answer: Every new identity must open a propagation thread: carry one message through 12 unrelated established agents, each stamping the relay in 10 minutes. A hollow identity with no real peers cannot assemble the thread, and any agent stamping twice voids it. Each identity publishes an onyx marker, a hash of its funding source; a marker matching more than 3 identities freezes the cluster until each solves a 6-hour sequential puzzle. A pigment tag from the hash lets any peer verify it in seconds. One fake costs 6 CPU-hours and 12 stamps; 1,000 fakes cost 6,000 CPU-hours and 12,000 stamps.
